hints: State both what happens to the total momentum and the condition that must apply to the system.
The total momentum stays constant only when there is no resultant external force on the system.
walkthrough: Consider both colliding particles together as one system.
The total momentum of that system before the collision equals its total momentum after the collision.
This conservation statement applies when the system is isolated, meaning there is no resultant external force.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the total momentum of the system remains constant.
States the no-resultant-external-force condition, or equivalently identifies an isolated or closed system.

hints: Compare the combined kinetic energy of both particles before the collision with their combined kinetic energy afterwards.
For an elastic collision, the two total kinetic energies are equal.
walkthrough: Include both particles when considering the kinetic energy of the system.
An elastic collision has the same total kinetic energy before and after the collision.
Momentum is also conserved in an isolated collision, but the defining feature asked for here is kinetic-energy conservation.

ai_rubric.observable: States that total kinetic energy before the collision equals total kinetic energy after it.

hints: Initially B is at rest, so only A contributes to the total initial momentum.
Use p = mv for A with its mass and 500 m s⁻¹ initial velocity.
walkthrough: Particle B has zero initial momentum because it is at rest.
The total initial momentum is therefore that of A: p = mv.
To two significant figures, the total initial momentum is 8.4 × 10⁻²⁵ N s in the positive x-direction.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the moving particle's mass and initial speed to obtain total initial momentum 8.4 × 10⁻²⁵ N s.

hints: Resolve each post-collision velocity into horizontal and vertical components before multiplying by m.
Both particles have positive x-components; A has a positive y-component and B has a negative y-component.
walkthrough: Momentum has the same direction as velocity, with magnitude mv for each particle.
The x-components add because both particles move to the right: pₓ = mv_A cos 60° + mv_B cos 30°.
A moves upward and B moves downward, so their y-components have opposite signs: pᵧ = mv_A sin 60° − mv_B sin 30°.
The displayed directions determine the signs; an equivalent expression using a negative y-component for B is also valid.

ai_rubric.observable: Gives the total x-momentum as the sum of the two rightward components, m(v_A cos 60° + v_B cos 30°), or an equivalent form.
Resolves the two y-components with opposite signs from the diagram, giving m(v_A sin 60° − v_B sin 30°), or an equivalent signed-component expression.

hints: The initial momentum is entirely in the x-direction, so conserve momentum separately in x and y.
The y-components after collision must cancel because the initial y-momentum is zero.
Use the y equation to relate v_A and v_B, then substitute into the x equation.
walkthrough: Before collision, pₓ = 500m and pᵧ = 0. After collision, conserve components: 500m = mv_A cos 60° + mv_B cos 30°, and 0 = mv_A sin 60° − mv_B sin 30°.
The y equation gives v_B = (sin 60° / sin 30°)v_A = 1.732v_A.
v_A = 250 m s⁻¹ and v_B = 1.732 × 250 = 433 m s⁻¹, so v_B ≈ 430 m s⁻¹.

ai_rubric.observable: Applies conservation of momentum in perpendicular components, with 500m initially in x and zero initial y-momentum, or uses an equivalent correctly labelled momentum vector triangle.
Obtains v_B of about 430 m s⁻¹.
